> Closed 2026-11-26: merged with the backup discussion into
> [2026-11-26-github.qmd](2026-11-26-github.qmd), one GitHub App for both.

Mocks of every screen, the badge styles and what was checked in libjami are on a page:
<https://claude.ai/artifact/LjmK3ewEgtoqeJS1XiMg5y>.

GitHub only (decided in conversation). No signing and no keys: the badge needs two
claims that name each other. A public gist `joma.json` in the GitHub account names the
Jami ID, and only that GitHub account can publish it (written once through the OAuth
device flow, scope `gist`, token thrown away). An `X-JOMA-GITHUB:<login>` line in the
Jami profile (vCard) names the GitHub account, and only that Jami account can send it.
Matching uses the numeric `github_id`, not the login.

Checked in `upstream/jami-daemon`:

- The profile is sent and stored as the file it is (`sendProfile`, `data_transfer.cpp:945`).
- `updateProfile` keeps unknown lines (`vcard.cpp` parses and writes every key). The key
  must not start with `FN` or `PHOTO` (`removeByKey` matches by prefix).
- Joma writes the line, then calls `updateProfile` to resend it to every contact.
- `sendTrustRequest` carries a payload (under 64 KB) that arrives with
  `IncomingTrustRequest`. Joma uses `addContact` today.
- Linking a new device rebuilds the profile from the name and photo only
  (`jamiaccount.cpp:1479`), so the line is dropped there.

# 1. The OAuth App

The device flow needs a GitHub OAuth App with device flow on. Its client ID ships in the
binary, and nothing else is secret. Proposal: you register "Joma" under your account.
Until then, only the by-hand path works (Joma copies the JSON and opens
gist.github.com).

- [ ] A:

# 2. Where setup lives

Proposal: a "verify with GitHub" button on the account row in the accounts tab, because
the proof belongs to one account. The steps run in the conversation tile: explain
(the gist is public), the code, publish. The alternative is a new "identity" section in
settings.

- [ ] A:

# 3. Badge style

A: check and `github.com/alice` in muted text. B: an accent pill "✓ GitHub".
C: a check on the avatar's corner. Proposal: A in the header and on the account row,
C in the lists.

- [ ] A:

# 4. Where it shows

Proposal: conversation header, chats and contacts lists, incoming requests, the add
card, the account row. The compact bar panel and the incoming-call overlay are optional.

- [ ] A:

# 5. Badge on incoming requests

Joma sends its vCard as the request payload (`sendTrustRequest`), so the receiver can
check before accepting. Proposal: yes. The Jami app sends profiles with requests too.

- [ ] A:

# 6. Adding by GitHub name

Proposal: a two-way switch above the add input (Jami name or ID / github, Tab flips),
plus `gh:alice` in the Jami field as a shortcut. A card shows what was found. Nothing is
sent before you confirm it. The alternative is two separate fields.

- [ ] A:

# 7. Several accounts

Proposal: one `joma.json` listing every account with a label. Verifying a second
account adds to the list. When adding, you pick from the list.

- [ ] A:

# 8. Re-checking

Proposal: every 3 days and whenever a profile arrives, with results cached (GitHub
allows 60 calls an hour without a login). A missing gist removes the badge with one
system line.

- [ ] A:

# 9. When the pinned pair changes

Proposal: a red banner in that conversation, no badge until you choose "trust the new
one", and nothing blocked.

- [ ] A:

# 10. Linked devices

Proposal: a new device puts the line back by itself when your gist already names this
account, with no new GitHub login.

- [ ] A:

# 11. Removing

Proposal: remove clears the profile line right away, then offers a second GitHub
approval to delete the gist. If you skip that, Joma opens the gist so you can delete it
yourself.

- [ ] A:

# 12. GitHub avatar on the add card

Proposal: no. Keep the Jami picture and link to the GitHub profile.
